summary: Guidance: configuring ephemeral probe accounting and client-side smoothing to prevent opaque 429s
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent 429 responses across several API routes during normal traffic spikes. The pattern is opaque (no consistent client-side spike) and appears correlated with background telemetry probes and a new signed-url callback flow launched last week.

Impact:
- Multiple client processes experience short-lived 429s (seconds to a couple minutes) during what the customer calls "routine telemetry sweeps".
- No clear console quota depletion; console shows available credits but requests still receive 429s.
- Affects their production ingest path for embeddings and a low-latency chat route. Customer worried about data loss and wants a recommended rate-limit configuration.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (dedicated) in prod-us-west.
- Running redwood-open-7b for chat and embeddings.
- Several short-lived signed URLs used for callback jobs; healthcheck sidecar added to ingestion workers last week.

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Start baseline worker farm (10 workers) with signed-url callback pattern (each worker requests signed URL, posts chunk, and polls for callback).
2) Enable the sidecar healthcheck (1s heartbeat) at worker level.
3) Launch scheduled telemetry sweep across all workers (one background job every 30s).
4) Observe spike window: some routes start returning 429s for a subset of ephemeral keys for ~30-90s.

Logs / Observations sent by customer:
- Sample request IDs: req_usw_20260312_1823a (chat), req_usw_20260312_1823b (embed), callback_req_1823c.
- Example response header (when 429 occurs): X-RateLimit-Reason: TOKEN_WINDOW_EXHAUSTED; X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0; X-Trace: trace-4be2
- Console screenshot shows remaining credits 74% for tenant and 100% for route (screenshot timestamps line up with 429 windows).

Customer asks:
- How should we account for short-lived healthchecks and telemetry probes so they don't cause opaque 429s?
- Should signed URL callbacks be separated into a different route or burst pool?
- What smoothing/refill configuration prevents brief synchronized drain from background probes and client warmups?
comments: 2026-03-12 14:02 - Maya Chen (Reporter): Adding logs and a timeline. We rolled out the sidecar healthcheck alongside a small UX release; spike started ~5 minutes after canary. Healthcheck is configured with a 1s interval and uses ephemeral auth tokens.\n

2026-03-12 18:10 - Support (Liam O'Connor): Thanks for the report. We're triaging — asking SRE to check refill pacing and any sudden token bucket drains. Can you confirm whether signed-url callbacks use the same API key as the workers? If not, please include the key prefixes.\n

2026-03-13 09:35 - Customer (Fleetly Labs - Priya Rao, Eng): Signed-url callbacks use the same tenant key but we create ephemeral tokens server-side per callback; we do not rotate the tenant-level API key. Callback traffic looks bursty (many short-lived posts after ingest completion).\n

2026-03-13 16:44 - SRE (Jordan Patel): Preliminary check: no global refill outage. Found short windows of token-window exhaustion on a route-weighted layer during telemetry sweeps. The tenant bucket had spare credits but per-route window dropped to zero due to many 1s healthchecks being attributed to the same route.\n
investigation_notes: Checked rate-limiter metrics (tenant/route layers) around provided req ids: trace-4be2 shows per-route bucket refilled every 60s while healthchecks consumed ~40 tokens/minute on that route, causing the route window to empty and reject until next refill.\n

Edge proxy attribution: healthcheck pings originate from worker IPs and reuse persistent HTTP/2 connections; ingress-sidecar set keepalive was causing many probes to be counted against the same connection/token window, amplifying drain.\n

Signed-url callbacks: since callbacks are short-lived and immediately follow successful uploads, they create a coincident microburst that aligns with the healthcheck timing, producing synchronized drain.\n

Console mismatch: console shows tenant-level credits (aggregated) but per-route/show-level windows can be exhausted independently — explainability gap: customer saw tenant credits >0 while route window was zero.\n

Related runbook: Confluence:RateLimiter-Runbook (section: route-isolation) clarifies per-route bucket behavior and burst pools. Linked PR for future telemetry: github.com/redwood-inference/rate-limiter/pull/642 introduces a telemetry-exempt flag for healthchecks (draft).\n
resolution: Workaround (applied 2026-03-13 20:12): Created a separate route for signed-url callbacks and moved healthcheck traffic to a dedicated telemetry route. This immediately removed the synchronized drain and stopped 429 windows.\n

Configuration guidance provided to customer:
- Create an isolated route for ephemeral callback and another for sidecar healthchecks; reserve a small burst pool for telemetry to avoid consuming main route token windows.
- Use longer healthcheck intervals (2-5s) or batch healthchecks at the sidecar to reduce per-second token consumption.
- Enable route-weighted burst pools: allocate a dedicated small refill interval for telemetry (e.g., 10 tokens/10s) while keeping main route refill untouched.
- If using ephemeral tokens for callbacks, tag them with a callback scope so they can be mapped to the telemetry route by the edge and not count against chat/embed windows.

Follow-ups (open):
- Engineering: investigate adding opt-in telemetry-exempt headers for healthchecks (related PR #642).
- Product: update console UI to surface per-route token windows more clearly for dedicated customers.
- Support: validate with customer that changes removed 429s and document recommended templates for telemetry/healthcheck configs.
